body.heading: Plant your seed
paragraphs: Soak a dry bean in water overnight with your adult's help. It will grow plump and wrinkly, like it is waking up.
Push the bean gently against the inside of a clear jar with damp paper towel or cotton wool around it, so you can see it through the glass.

body.heading: Watch each day
paragraphs: Put the jar somewhere light, but not in hot direct sun. Check it every day. First you may see a tiny white root poke out.
Then a green shoot will reach up towards the light. Draw what you see each day. Growing is slow, and that is part of the fun.

body.heading: What the seed is doing
paragraphs: A seed is a baby plant with a packed lunch inside. The water wakes it up, and it eats its lunch while it grows roots and leaves.
When your shoot has leaves, your adult can help you move it into soil in a pot, where it can keep growing.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: grow a bean in a clear jar and watch its roots and shoot appear day by day.
